c.n: Our group hosts the Court of Master Sommeliers L
c.s: Our group hosts the Court of Master Sommeliers Level 1 and Level 2 at Testa Barra. This is your guide: what the Court is, why to sign up, and how to get ready.

c.n: Dates from the Court’s calendar on Oct 31, 2026.

c.s: Level 1 covers the major regions and grapes, how wine is made, food pairing, beer, sake and spirits. That’s most of what guests ask at the table.

c.s: The Court says the Certified Sommelier title “is well recognized in the hospitality sector globally,” and the pin tells an employer and guests your skills were tested.

c.s: The Court lists server, bartender and support roles for Level 1, and lead server, captain, assistant floor sommelier, bartender and manager for Level 2.

c.s: Every French wine sits in one of three tiers. The top tier, AOC, began in 1935; AOP is the same thing under EU law (since 1992).

c.n: The most northerly vineyard in France, about 150
c.s: The most northerly vineyard in France, about 150 km north-east of Paris. Cool, with both oceanic and continental influences. Chalk soils store water.

c.s: Most Champagne is white, though two of its three grapes are black.

c.s: Non-vintage: at least 15 months before release. Vintage: at least 3 years.

c.n: Mainly temperate where continental, oceanic and
c.s: Mainly temperate where continental, oceanic and southern influences meet. Chablis in the north is colder, with spring frost; the Mâconnais in the south is warmer.

c.n: Red Burgundy is Pinot Noir; white Burgundy is Ch
c.s: Red Burgundy is Pinot Noir; white Burgundy is Chardonnay.

c.n: Chablis: one colour, one grape (Chardonnay), Kim
c.s: Chablis: one colour, one grape (Chardonnay), Kimmeridgian limestone with tiny oyster fossils.

c.n: Beaujolais is almost all Gamay (97%), with 10 cr
c.s: Beaujolais is almost all Gamay (97%), with 10 crus. Nouveau comes out the third Thursday of November.

c.s: Burgundy has 84 AOCs, more than any other French region.

c.s: On the Atlantic coast in the south-west: maritime near the ocean, more continental inland. Three rivers shape it: the Gironde, the Garonne and the Dordogne.

c.s: France’s longest river. Oceanic near Nantes and the coast, more continental heading inland. White is the main colour.

c.n: Between the Rhine and the Vosges mountains. The
c.s: Between the Rhine and the Vosges mountains. The Vosges block rain from the west, so Alsace is one of the driest, sunniest parts of France.

c.n: More than 90% of Alsace wine is white.
c.s: More than 90% of Alsace wine is white.

c.n: Wines are named for the grape, and a named grape
c.s: Wines are named for the grape, and a named grape means 100% that grape.

c.s: Crémant d’Alsace is the sparkling wine: about a quarter of production.

c.n: Each its own appellation, about 5% of the wine.
c.s: Each its own appellation, about 5% of the wine. The classic Grand Cru grapes: Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat.

c.n: Only berries with noble rot, picked by hand.
c.s: Only berries with noble rot, picked by hand.

c.n: Two halves, 30 miles apart. The north is steep a
c.s: Two halves, 30 miles apart. The north is steep and continental. The south is Mediterranean and flatter, dried by the Mistral, a cold north wind.

c.n: A cru is one village and one AOC, the top of the
c.s: A cru is one village and one AOC, the top of the Rhône ladder.

c.n: Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise is a Vin Doux Nature
c.s: Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise is a Vin Doux Naturel: alcohol added to stop the fermentation.

c.s: Ladder: Côtes du Rhône, then Côtes du Rhône Villages, then the crus.
